summary: What the battle window hides of a unit the player knows little of: only the type picture of a land unit's entry, which becomes GFX_counter_unknown (a '?' box) where CUnit +0x1F8 intel_level is under 3 - the map counter's own picture test, inlined. Name, bars, location, width strip and tooltip are never masked; ships and wings never. The static default key at VA 0x170D858 is the string 'unknown', set by a CRT initialiser. Corrects 'oob_level >= 3' in the CUnitOption record and the battle row's 'no type key under 3'.

addresses.name: CUnitOption::CUnitOption
addresses.no_signature: a constructor: the GUI's factory in ECX and five on the stack - the object, the unit, whether its side attacks, the parent and the view - `ret 0x14`, and a returned `this`; not typed
addresses.comment: **A unit's entry in a list of the battle window**, from the window `division_option`. `counter_type` takes the sprite GFX_counter_<key of the first brigade's type> where the unit's **intel_level (CUnit +0x1F8) is 3 or more** and it has a brigade with a type, and **GFX_counter_unknown** otherwise (the key is the static g_UnknownCounterKey, 'unknown') - the same test as CUnit_GetCounterTypeKey, inlined (0x729668 `cmp [esi+0x1F8],3; jl`); set only where a sprite of that name exists, else the file's GFX_temp_unit_icon stays. **This is the only thing in a land unit's entry the player's knowledge changes**: `name`, the bars, `location` and the width strip are written whatever the intel level, and the picture is set here alone, never by CUnitOption::Update, so it keeps the level of the moment the entry was made. `unit_cw_strip` a frame by the unit's width - 1 under 2, 2 under 4, 3 under 6, 4 under 8, 5 from 8; `combat_unit_bg`, a progress bar, 100; `name` the unit's name (CUnit slot 7, the string at +0x16C, no test). Then CUnitOption::Update. Group `army_option`. *Corrected 2026-11-13: this said 'a unit at division level or below'; +0x1F8 is the intel level, not the order of battle level.* See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-combatview.md, section 5.
addresses.revises: the counter picture's test is the intel level (+0x1F8 >= 3), not 'division level or below'; the default is GFX_counter_unknown; nothing else in the entry is masked
addresses.evidence: Listing 0x729611..0x72968B: the unit is [ebp+0xC] (pushed to the reference set 0x42DD70 at 0x729614), then `cmp dword ptr [esi+0x1F8],3; jl 0x72968B`, `cmp [esi+0x40],0; jle`, first node, `[data+0x58]`, `+8`, else `mov eax,0x170D858` - byte for byte CUnit_GetCounterTypeKey (0x5BDB60). CUnit +0x1F8 is recorded intel_level. A cfg walk of this function, CUnitOption::Update, CCombatView::FillUnitList/UpdateSide/BuildTooltip/BuildUnitTooltip and the ship and wing entries and their direct callees finds this one 0x1F8 read and no call to 0x5BDB60, 0x5BE500, 0x84AD10, 0x84AEB0 or 0x5D37D0 (positive control: the walk of FillUnitList finds this read through its callee). The name is CUnit slot 7 = 0x5C47A0, a plain copy of +0x16C. What would show it wrong: a virtual call in the entry routines reaching an intel test (window and unit slots were spot-checked, not all followed), or a running game showing the name replaced.

addresses.name: CUnitOption::Update
addresses.comment: **Refreshes a unit's entry**: `str_bar` is the brigades' strengths added up over the unit's full strength (slot 24), `org_bar` its average organisation (slot 20) over its summed definition's max_organisation, each a whole number of hundredths; `location` the name of its province; and for a unit landing from the sea `combat_unit_bg` is how far the landing has got. **No test of the player's intel level**: an enemy unit's bars and province are shown in full however little is known of it, and the counter picture is not touched here (CUnitOption::CUnitOption alone sets it). Slot 8. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-combatview.md, section 5.
addresses.revises: comment only: adds that nothing here depends on the intel level and that the picture is not refreshed
addresses.evidence: cfg walk of 0x7299B0 (317 instructions, to 0x729D32): no operand with displacement 0x1F8, no call to an intel-gated helper; its direct callees likewise; its indirect calls are the unit's slots 23 and 20 (0x5C6520, 0x5C6580 - neither reads 0x1F8), the province's name slot and window slots +0x44/+0x48. What would show it wrong: an intel test behind one of those virtual calls.

addresses.name: CUnit_GetCounterTypeKey
addresses.comment: **Which unit type a counter shows**: the key of the unit's FIRST brigade's type (`regiments.first->data->definition + 8`) where its intel level (+0x1F8) is above 2 and it has a brigade; otherwise g_UnknownCounterKey (VA 0x170D858), **the string 'unknown'** - empty in the file, set at startup by UnknownCounterKey_Init - so the picture is GFX_small_counter_unknown / GFX_map_counter_unknown, a box with a question mark. The same test is inlined in CUnitOption::CUnitOption (the battle window's entry) and CombatSide_UnitNames (a battle row's `£` icon). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-counters.md and reversing/findings/FINDINGS-combatview.md.
addresses.revises: comment only: the run-time value of the static default is 'unknown', and the test is inlined in two battle routines
addresses.evidence: 0xCC4510 is `push 7; push 0x15C80A8 ('unknown'); mov ecx,0x170D858; call 0x40A160 (std::string assign); push 0xD22A60; call atexit; ret`, and its address is a dword at VA 0xD4022C in .rdata, the CRT initialiser table. The 22 references to 0x170D858 in .text are that store, the destructor at 0xD22A60 (two references) and 19 `mov reg,0x170D858` fallbacks of this same shape - no other writer. What would show it wrong: a write to 0x170D858 through a pointer a scan cannot see.

addresses.name: CombatSide_UnitNames
addresses.signature: Hoi3CString* __stdcall CombatSide_UnitNames(void* units@ECX, Hoi3CString* out@stack:4, int limit@stack:8) @EAX
addresses.comment: A side's units by name: '@' tag ' £' first brigade's type key ' ' name, joined ', ' and ' AND '; a fleet's or air unit's ships or wings each with the unit's own name, run together. **A land unit whose intel level (CUnit +0x1F8) is under 3, or that has no brigade with a type, gets the key 'unknown'** (g_UnknownCounterKey) and so the unknown counter's picture; its tag and name are written all the same. The ships' and wings' arm has no such test. Under a limit of 21 one to a line, cut to 20 letters, AND_MORE past it. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-battletooltips.md and reversing/findings/FINDINGS-combatview.md.
addresses.revises: comment only: the type key is gated on the intel level and falls back to 'unknown', not to nothing
addresses.evidence: Listing 0x56F7D7..0x56F808: `cmp dword ptr [edi+0x1F8],3; jl 0x56F7FA` ... `mov ecx,0x170D858` pushed to the concatenation at 0x56F808 in place of the type key. A cfg walk of the whole function (to 0x5703DC; the next function is 0x5703E0) finds no second 0x1F8 read. What would show it wrong: g_UnknownCounterKey holding something else at run time.

addresses.name: UnknownCounterKey_Init
addresses.comment: The `.CRT$XCU` initialiser that sets **g_UnknownCounterKey** (rva 0x130D858) to the std::string 'unknown' (the literal at rva 0x11C80A8) and registers its destructor (rva 0x922A60) with atexit. Its address is in the CRT initialiser table at rva 0x94022C. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-combatview.md.
addresses.evidence: Disassembled whole, 0xCC4510..0xCC452C, bare `ret`, three int3 after; findValue of 0xCC4510 over .rdata answers exactly 0xD4022C. What would show it wrong: nothing reachable - the bytes are the claim.

addresses.name: g_UnknownCounterKey
addresses.comment: **A std::string (Hoi3CString, 0x1C bytes) holding 'unknown'** at run time; empty in the file (capacity 15 at +0x14), written once by UnknownCounterKey_Init. The fallback type key wherever a unit's counter is drawn and the player's intel level on it is under 3 or it has no brigade with a type: CUnit_GetCounterTypeKey (the map's counters), CUnitOption::CUnitOption (the battle window's entry, GFX_counter_unknown), CombatSide_UnitNames (a battle row's `£unknown`), and 16 more fallbacks of the same shape (`... ? definition + 8 : this`) that were not read. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-combatview.md.
addresses.evidence: Bytes at VA 0x170D858 read 16 zeros, length 0, capacity 0xF - an empty SSO std::string; the only store is the initialiser's assign at 0xCC4517; the destructor at 0xD22A60 frees +0 when +0x14 >= 0x10. The 16 other readers were listed by findRefs and not read. What would show it wrong: a store through a computed pointer.

struct_fields.name: intel_level
struct_fields.comment: **How well the screen's country knows this unit**: 9 for its own units and its friends' (the same real faction, or an alliance in the owner's status towards it), else the byte of `intel_by_country` for it in the province the unit is in (0 unseen, 3 partial, 9 own). Written by CUnit::EnterProvince and **every hour for every unit of every country by RunHourlyTick** (0x6822C8..0x6823D7), which sets the avatar's rebuild byte (+0x10C) where it changed. Under 2 its stack is not drawn, under 3 its counter shows the unknown picture, under 5 its name is `???`, under 7 its two figures are `?`. **In a battle only the under-3 picture test is repeated**: CUnitOption::CUnitOption gives a land unit's entry GFX_counter_unknown and CombatSide_UnitNames gives a battle row `£unknown` (both inline copies of CUnit_GetCounterTypeKey); no battle element shows `???` or `?` for it (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-combatview.md).
struct_fields.revises: comment only: adds the two battle readers and that the name and figure thresholds have no counterpart there
struct_fields.evidence: The two reads at 0x729668 and 0x56F7D7, both `cmp [reg+0x1F8],3; jl`; the battle window's routines scanned as in the CUnitOption::CUnitOption entry. What would show it wrong: another read in the combat view reached only through a virtual call.
